title: The Choir's Quiet Experiment
titleZh: 合唱团悄然开展的实验
paras: At a neighbourhood choir housed in a converted bakery, coordinator Mira Sen investigated why new volunteers frequently disappeared after their first concert. Although registered as a charitable [[entity|entity]], the choir depended entirely on unpaid labour. Interviews suggested that musical anxiety mattered less than uncertainty about responsibilities, particularly when experienced members gave contradictory instructions.

Sen therefore devised an experiment involving twenty-four recruits, allocated by lottery to two groups. One received the usual verbal [[induction|induction]]; the other rehearsed practical tasks with a [[vocalist|vocalist]] named Tomas Vidal. These recruits learned where to [[stow|stow]] microphone stands and how to record borrowed equipment. To [[accustom|accustom]] them to unexpected demands, Vidal also simulated a missing cable. Both groups received identical written guidance.

For six weeks, observers recorded requests for assistance and reconstructed the [[chronology|chronology]] of each equipment failure. The choir's previously [[lax|lax]] record-keeping had made newcomers appear unusually [[prone|prone]] to mistakes, although misplaced objects often predated their arrival. Recruits who had practised the tasks asked fewer procedural questions, yet reported more faults before performances. This distinction mattered: silence was not necessarily evidence of competence, while reporting trouble could indicate growing confidence.

Practical preparation initially seemed an [[extravagance|extravagance]], since it required hiring the rehearsal room for another evening. However, participants found subsequent duties less [[burdensome|burdensome]], and ten remained after three concerts, compared with six in the other group. The small sample prevented sweeping conclusions, but it challenged a cherished assumption: commitment did not simply precede useful work; clear, manageable work could help commitment develop.
zh: 在一支以改建后的面包房为活动场所的社区合唱团里，协调员米拉·森调查了新志愿者为何常常在首场音乐会后便不再露面。合唱团虽注册为慈善机构，却完全依靠无偿劳动运作。访谈表明，相比对音乐表现的焦虑，职责不明确的影响更大，尤其是当资深成员给出的指示相互矛盾时。
因此，森设计了一项实验，将二十四名新成员抽签分为两组。一组接受常规的口头入职培训；另一组则与歌手托马斯·维达尔一起演练实际任务。这些新成员学习了麦克风支架应收在哪里，以及如何登记借来的器材。为了让他们习惯应对突发需求，维达尔还模拟了电缆丢失的情况。两组收到的书面指南完全相同。
在六周内，观察员记录了求助情况，并还原了每次器材故障发生的时间顺序。合唱团以往松懈的记录管理，让新成员显得格外容易出错，尽管物品放错位置往往发生在他们加入之前。演练过任务的新成员提出的流程性问题更少，却在演出前报告了更多故障。这一区别很重要：沉默未必意味着胜任，而报告问题则可能表明信心正在增强。
实际操作培训起初似乎是一种浪费，因为这需要额外租用排练室一个晚上。然而，参与培训的人觉得后续职责不再那么繁重，三场音乐会后仍有十人留下，而另一组只剩六人。样本较小，无法据此得出普遍结论，但实验挑战了一个备受推崇的假设：投入感并非只会先于有效工作而产生；清晰、可承担的工作也能帮助培养投入感。

q.s: Sen interviewed every volunteer who had left after their first concert.
q.why: 文章未说明访谈是否涵盖所有离开的志愿者。

q.s: Both groups were given the same written guidance.
q.why: 第二段明确说两组收到相同的书面指南。

q.s: Recruits given practical training reported fewer equipment problems before concerts.
q.why: 实际演练组在演出前报告了更多故障。
